name: Dual Kettlebell Press
description: The dual kettlebell overhead press is performed with two kettlebells racked in the front-rack position, pressing both simultaneously overhead. The racked position places the kettlebells against the forearms with the bells resting on the shoulder girdle, which requires unique shoulder positioning and upper body tension compared to dumbbell pressing. The simultaneous bilateral load demands greater core bracing against the compressed, weighted rack position.

execution.starting_position: Clean two kettlebells to the front-rack position: bells resting on the forearms and upper arms, elbows pointing slightly forward and down. Feet hip-width apart, core braced.
execution.setup_instructions: Learning the kettlebell front-rack position is prerequisite — it differs substantially from a barbell rack. Practice with lighter kettlebells first.
steps: Step 1: Clean both kettlebells to the front-rack position.
Step 2: Brace the core and set the feet.
Step 3: Press both kettlebells overhead simultaneously, keeping them in a vertical path.
Step 4: At lockout, arms fully extended with the bells directly above the shoulders.
Step 5: Lower both under control to the front-rack position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the press, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows wide in the rack — elbows should point forward and down, not to the sides
Pressing one side before the other — the press should be simultaneous
safety_considerations: Learn the front-rack position before adding heavy loads
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Front-rack position to full overhead lockout.
coaching_cues: Rack them tight — bells on the forearms
